done_when: When close's merge of the default branch conflicts only in files forge sync writes, close takes the default branch's copy of those files, re-runs sync, commits the merge and continues; a conflict in any other file still stops close as today. New and existing repos: works in any repo on this release, since it uses the repo's own sync output. One command-level test: two branches that both changed the skill template merge through close without stopping, and a conflict in a code file still stops it.

findings.body: The earlier finding remains open. When close runs using the conflicted Forge worktree's source, passing the clean default tree does not isolate the inventory scan: src/forge/sync.py:317–322 reads and parses modules under forge.__path__. A conflict in src/forge/*.py therefore raises SyntaxError before merge --abort and the normal conflict instructions run. The checkout remains in an active merge, and subsequent Forge commands cannot parse it (src/forge/cli.py:37–43). Classify these conflicts before scanning live modules, or abort the merge when inventory construction fails.
findings.title: Abort source-code conflicts before scanning live Forge modules

findings.body: The earlier finding remains open. src/forge/githooks.py:74 includes CLAUDE.md in sync's inventory only when it exists. If default-branch sync deleted it while the worker modified it, this inventory omits the modify/delete conflict and close incorrectly refuses recovery. The same omission affects staging at close.py:290: when only the worker added CLAUDE.md, recovery for another generated conflict runs sync and deletes it, but filters its deletion out of staging. The merge then retains obsolete content and leaves the checkout dirty. Include sync-managed deletion paths even when absent from the default tree.
findings.title: Include sync-managed deletions absent from the default tree

why: When forge close merges the default branch, the copies of the skill and guide that forge sync writes conflict on almost every busy day, and close stops until someone takes main's copy and re-runs sync by hand
